claim: The mouse MOE is divided into a limited series of stereotypic segments based on the expression of OR genes that exhibit bilateral symmetry between the two nasal cavities.
source: The mouse MOE is divided into a limited series of stereotypic segments, based on the expression of OR genes, that exhibit bilateral symmetry between the two nasal cavities (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 1A showing the zonal organization.

claim: OR transcription starts in neuronal progenitors of the main olfactory epithelium, which transiently express 5–15 ORs out of >1000 OR genes distributed in genomic clusters across chromosomes.
source: OR transcription starts in neuronal progenitors of the main olfactory epithelium (MOE), which transiently express 5–15 ORs out of >1000 OR genes distributed in genomic clusters across chromosomes (Hanchate et al., 2015; Tan et al., 2015; Saraiva et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Hanchate et al., 2015; Tan et al., 2015; Saraiva et al., 2015).

claim: As progenitor cells differentiate into post-mitotic olfactory sensory neurons, they switch from polygenic to monogenic and monoallelic OR transcription.
source: As these progenitor cells differentiate into post-mitotic olfactory sensory neurons (OSNs), they switch from polygenic to monogenic and monoallelic OR transcription (Chess et al., 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chess et al., 1994.

claim: The transition from polygenic to monogenic OR transcription is mediated by the assembly of a multi-chromosomal enhancer hub over the chosen OR allele.
source: This transition is mediated by the assembly of a multi-chromosomal enhancer hub over the chosen OR allele (Lomvardas et al., 2006; Markenscoff-Papadimitriou et al., 2014; Monahan et al., 2019), followed by the stabilizing effects of an OR-elicited feedback signal (Lyons et al., 2013; Dalton et al., 2013; Serizawa et al., 2005; Shykind et al., 2004; Lewcock and Reed, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Heterochromatic silencing and genomic OR compartmentalization act together to assure that non-chosen OR alleles remain transcriptionally repressed for the life of the OSN.
source: During this developmental progression, heterochromatic silencing (Magklara et al., 2011) and genomic OR compartmentalization (Clowney et al., 2012; Le Gros et al., 2016) act together to assure that the non-chosen OR alleles will remain transcriptionally repressed for the life of the OSN.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Magklara et al., 2011; Clowney et al., 2012; Le Gros et al., 2016).

claim: The position of the OSN across the dorsoventral axis of the MOE predisposes singular transcriptional choice towards a group of 50–250 OR genes.
source: Interestingly, the position of the OSN across the dorsoventral (DV) axis of the MOE predisposes this singular transcriptional choice towards a group of 50–250 OR genes (Tan and Xie, 2018), providing reproducible topographic restrictions in OR expression.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tan and Xie, 2018.

claim: The anatomical segments of the MOE that express a specific collection of OR identities are known as 'zones,' with their total number varying from 4 to 9.
source: The anatomical segments of the MOE that express a specific collection of OR identities are known as 'zones,' with their total number varying from 4 to 9, depending on the analyses and criteria used to define them (Ressler et al., 1993; Vassar et al., 1993; Miyamichi et al., 2005; Zapiec and Mombaerts, 2020; Ruiz Tejada Segura et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Zonal restrictions in OR expression have a well-established influence on the wiring of the olfactory circuit.
source: Although zonal restrictions in OR expression have a well-established influence on the wiring of the olfactory circuit (Sullivan et al., 1994; Sullivan et al., 1995), the mechanisms that bias this singular transcriptional choice towards specific OR identities remain unknown.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Sullivan et al., 1994 and Sullivan et al., 1995.

claim: OR expression is first detected in INP3 cells.
source: Olfactory receptor expression is first detected in INP3 cells (right panel).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Dorsally positioned INPs transcribe almost exclusively dorsal identity ORs.
source: Surprisingly, while dorsally positioned INPs transcribe almost exclusively dorsal identity ORs, ventrally positioned INPs transcribe complex mixtures consisting of ORs of every zonal identity (Figure 1C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1C-D.

claim: Ventrally positioned INPs transcribe complex mixtures consisting of ORs of every zonal identity.
source: Surprisingly, while dorsally positioned INPs transcribe almost exclusively dorsal identity ORs, ventrally positioned INPs transcribe complex mixtures consisting of ORs of every zonal identity (Figure 1C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1C-D.

claim: Ventral INPs transcribe a greater number of OR genes compared to dorsal INPs.
source: Overall, ventral INPs transcribe a greater number of OR genes compared to dorsal INPs.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text based on analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data.

claim: Dorsal identity ORs are detected in 43 ventral INP cells while ventral identity ORs are detected in only 29 of them.
source: Focusing on OR genes detected with at least three unique transcripts, we detect dorsal identity ORs in 43 ventral INP cells and ventral identity ORs in only 29 of them, while dorsal INP cells express predominantly dorsal ORs (Figure 1C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1C-D.

claim: As ventral INPs differentiate to iOSNs, dorsal identity OR transcription is replaced by the 'correct' (zone-appropriate) ventral OR transcription.
source: Moreover, as the ventral INPs differentiate to iOSNs, dorsal identity OR transcription is replaced by the 'correct' (zone-appropriate) ventral OR transcription, culminating in singular expression of an OR allele with the correct zonal identity in mOSNs (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: In every MOE segment, INPs co-transcribe ORs with the correct as well as more dorsal zonal identities.
source: This bulk analysis showed that in every case INPs co-transcribe ORs with the correct as well as more dorsal zonal identities, while further differentiation replaces dorsal ORs with ORs of the correct identity (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by bulk RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: OSN differentiation coincides with heterochromatin-mediated OR gene silencing.
source: We previously showed that OSN differentiation coincides with heterochromatin-mediated OR gene silencing (Magklara et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Magklara et al., 2011).

claim: Dorsal-most identity (zone 1) ORs have the highest levels of heterochromatin.
source: We predicted that dorsal-most identity (zone 1) ORs, which are expressed in INPs throughout the MOE, should have the highest levels of heterochromatin, whereas ventral-most identity (zone 5) ORs, which are transcribed only in ventral INPs, should have the lowest, with the rest of the OR repertoire having intermediate levels of heterochromatin marks.
evidence: This is a prediction stated in the text that is then confirmed by experimental data.

claim: Ventral-most identity (zone 5) ORs have the lowest levels of heterochromatin.
source: We predicted that dorsal-most identity (zone 1) ORs, which are expressed in INPs throughout the MOE, should have the highest levels of heterochromatin, whereas ventral-most identity (zone 5) ORs, which are transcribed only in ventral INPs, should have the lowest, with the rest of the OR repertoire having intermediate levels of heterochromatin marks.
evidence: This is a prediction stated in the text that is then confirmed by experimental data.

claim: Visual inspection of ChIP-seq genomic tracks along OR gene clusters reveals the highest H3K9me3/H3K79me3 levels on dorsal identity OR genes and the lowest on ventral identity OR genes.
source: Indeed, visual inspection of ChIP-seq genomic tracks along OR gene clusters with mixed zonal constitution reveals the highest H3K9me3/H3K79me3 levels on the dorsal identity OR genes and the lowest on the ventral identity OR genes of the cluster (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Aggregate ChIP-seq analysis shows gradual reduction of H3K9me3 and H3K79me3 enrichment from dorsal to ventral ORs for the whole OR repertoire.
source: Aggregate ChIP-seq analysis of all the OR genes grouped by their zonal identities corroborates the gradual reduction of H3K9me3 and H3K79me3 enrichment from dorsal to ventral ORs for the whole OR repertoire (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Class I ORs do not follow the pattern of heterochromatin enrichment observed for canonical class II ORs.
source: The only exception from this pattern is found at the dorsally expressed class I ORs, which rely on different regulatory mechanisms than the canonical class II ORs (Hirota et al., 2007; Enomoto et al., 2019; Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to previous studies and supported by data in Figure 2B.

claim: Both H3K9me3 and H3K79me3 heterochromatic marks are predominantly deposited during the INP to iOSN transition.
source: Finally, using the FACS-based strategy described earlier, we confirmed that both heterochromatic marks are predominantly deposited during the INP to iOSN transition, simultaneously with the transition from polygenic to singular, zonally appropriate OR expression (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The descending pattern of heterochromatin enrichment from dorsal to ventral OR identities is preserved throughout differentiation.
source: Importantly, the descending pattern of heterochromatin enrichment from dorsal to ventral OR identities is preserved throughout differentiation.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on analysis of ChIP-seq data across developmental stages.

claim: In each MOE segment, OR genes with either the correct or more dorsal zonal identities have higher levels of heterochromatin compared to more ventral identity ORs.
source: In each segment, OR genes with either the correct or more dorsal zonal identities had a higher level of heterochromatin compared to more ventral identity ORs (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Most OR genes are heterochromatic in ventral OSNs.
source: Thus, most OR genes are heterochromatic in ventral OSNs; dorsal and dorsomedial identity OR genes are heterochromatic in dorsomedial OSNs; and only dorsal identity OR genes have some heterochromatin in dorsal OSNs (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Each zonal identity OR group has lower heterochromatin levels in the MOE segment where it is expressed by mOSNs compared to more ventral segments.
source: Although each zonal identity OR group is heterochromatic in the MOE segment where it is expressed by mOSNs, the level of H3K9me3/H3K79me3 enrichment is lower than in more ventral segments, where it is not chosen for stable expression.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on analysis of ChIP-seq data from different MOE segments.

claim: In a pure population of ventral mOSNs expressing Olfr1507, the remaining non-chosen zone 5 identity OR genes are silenced with the same level of heterochromatin as OR genes with more dorsal zonal identities.
source: Thus, in a pure population of ventral mOSNs expressing Olfr1507 (a ventral, zone 5 identity OR), the remaining non-chosen zone 5 identity OR genes are silenced with the same level of heterochromatin as OR genes with more dorsal zonal identities (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: In every MOE segment, OR heterochromatinization is preserved only for the ORs that have the potential to be expressed and is not applied to more ventral ORs.
source: In other words, in every MOE segment, OR heterochromatinization is preserved only for the ORs that have the potential to be expressed and is not applied to more ventral ORs, which were not transcriptionally active in INPs.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a conclusion from the ChIP-seq data analysis.

claim: Heterochromatin marks are detected on trace amine-associated receptor (TAAR) genes only in TAAR-expressing OSNs and not the rest of the MOE.
source: This is consistent with recent reports of heterochromatin marks being detected on trace amine-associated receptor (TAAR) genes only in TAAR-expressing OSNs and not the rest of the MOE (Fei et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Fei et al., 2021.

claim: Heterochromatic OR genes converge into multi-chromosomal genomic aggregates of extreme chromatin compaction that contribute to effective and stable silencing of non-chosen ORs.
source: Heterochromatic OR genes converge into multi-chromosomal genomic aggregates of extreme chromatin compaction that contribute to the effective and stable silencing of non-chosen ORs (Clowney et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Clowney et al., 2012.

claim: There is a striking resemblance between the deposition of heterochromatic marks on OR genes and genomic compartmentalization.
source: We saw a striking resemblance between the deposition of heterochromatic marks on OR genes and genomic compartmentalization (Figure 3A–B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Hi-C data shown in Figure 3A-B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: A cluster of predominately ventral identity OR genes is recruited to OR compartments only in ventral OSNs, where they are heterochromatic.
source: For example, inspection of the long range cis genomic interactions between 3 OR gene clusters on chromosome 2 shows that a cluster of predominately ventral identity OR genes is recruited to OR compartments only in ventral OSNs, where they are heterochromatic (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Hi-C data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Interactions between dorsal OR genes is the default in every OSN.
source: This analysis yielded the same conclusion: Interactions between dorsal OR genes is the default in every OSN, whereas compartmentalization for the remaining of the OR repertoire increases along the DV axis of the MOE (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Hi-C data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Compartmentalization for the remaining of the OR repertoire increases along the DV axis of the MOE.
source: This analysis yielded the same conclusion: Interactions between dorsal OR genes is the default in every OSN, whereas compartmentalization for the remaining of the OR repertoire increases along the DV axis of the MOE (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Hi-C data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Every OR has intermediate Hi-C contact frequencies with other OR genes in their segment of expression in the MOE, lower Hi-C contact frequencies in more dorsal MOE segments, and higher Hi-C contacts in more ventral segments.
source: Intriguingly, as with levels of heterochromatin, we detect the following recurrent pattern of OR compartmentalization: every OR has intermediate Hi-C contact frequencies with other OR genes in their segment of expression in the MOE, lower Hi-C contact frequencies in more dorsal MOE segments, and higher Hi-C contacts in more ventral segments.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on analysis of Hi-C data from different MOE segments.

claim: OR compartments in ventral mOSNs are larger and contain more OR genes from more chromosomes than in dorsal mOSNs.
source: We confirmed that OR compartments in ventral mOSNs are larger and contain more OR genes from more chromosomes than in dorsal mOSNs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Dip-C data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: In each ventral mOSN, significantly fewer ventral identity OR genes are found in OR compartments compared to dorsal or dorsomedial identity OR genes.
source: Importantly, in each cell, significantly fewer ventral identity OR genes were found in OR compartments compared to dorsal (zone 1) or dorsomedial (zone 2–3) identity OR genes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Dip-C data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: OR compartmentalization is highly probabilistic, with each one of the 48 dorsal and ventral OSNs having unique maps of OR-OR genomic interactions.
source: In this note, OR compartmentalization is highly probabilistic, with each one of the 48 dorsal and ventral OSNs having unique maps of OR-OR genomic interactions (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Dip-C data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: NFI paralogues Nfia, Nfib, and Nfix have strong, DV-influenced expression in INPs that is preserved in iOSNs.
source: NFI paralogues Nfia, Nfib, and Nfix have strong, DV-influenced expression in INPs that is preserved in iOSNs (Figure 4A and B and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: Nfia and Nfib are expressed higher in ventral INPs and iOSNs.
source: Specifically, Nfia and Nfib are expressed higher in ventral INPs and iOSNs, and Nfix is higher in ventral mOSNs (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Nfix is expressed higher in ventral mOSNs.
source: Specifically, Nfia and Nfib are expressed higher in ventral INPs and iOSNs, and Nfix is higher in ventral mOSNs (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: NFI transcription factors were previously implicated in OSN differentiation.
source: These three members of the nuclear factor I (NFI) family of transcription factors control a plethora of developmental and cell specification processes (Gronostajski, 2000; Zenker et al., 2019), and were previously implicated in OSN differentiation (Baumeister et al., 1999; Behrens et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Baumeister et al., 1999; Behrens et al., 2000).

claim: Triple NFI deletion in OSN progenitors results in significant transcriptional reduction of ventral OR identities and reciprocal increase of dorsomedial ORs.
source: RNA-seq analysis of the FAC-sorted cKO OSNs from the whole MOE revealed significant transcriptional reduction of ventral OR identities and reciprocal increase of dorsomedial ORs (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Triple NFI deletion only in mOSNs has no measurable effects on OR expression.
source: In contrast, triple NFI deletion only in mOSNs, using the Omp-IRES-Cre driver, has no measurable effects on OR expression (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Triple NFI deletion in ventral OSN progenitors results in ectopic expression of OR genes with dorsomedial zonal identities in place of OR genes with proper ventral ones.
source: This experiment revealed ectopic expression of OR genes with dorsomedial zonal identities in place of the OR genes with proper ventral ones (Figure 4E), a result confirmed by immunofluorescence (IF) experiments (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4E and IF data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D-E.

claim: Only 13 out of ~200 OSN-specific genes are significantly different with at least a twofold change between control and triple NFI cKO OSNs.
source: Only 13 out of ~200 OSN-specific genes are significantly different with at least a twofold change between control and cKO OSNs, and 113/207 non-OR ventral markers are still highly expressed in the ventral-most zones, acting as independent fiducial markers for our zonal dissection (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The severity of dorsomedial transformation in ventral mOSNs depends on the total number of NFI alleles deleted.
source: In fact, the severity of this dorsomedial transformation depends on the total number of NFI alleles deleted, with the triple Nfia, Nfib, Nfix deletion (NFI ABX cKO) mOSNs expressing predominantly zone 2 and 3 ORs, double Nfia, Nfib deletion (NFI AB cKO) mOSNs expressing zone 3 and 4 ORs, and single Nfix deletion (NFIX cKO) mOSNs having almost wild type expression patterns of zone 4 and 5 ORs (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Unbiased clustering of spatial transcriptomics data generated OR clusters that correspond to zonal patterns of OR expression in control MOEs.
source: Interestingly, while dimensionality reduction and unbiased clustering generated OR clusters that correspond to zonal patterns of OR expression (i.e. each cluster contains OR genes with one zonal identity) in control MOEs, only dorsal-most zone 1/class I OR genes followed this correlation in cKO MOEs (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by spatial transcriptomics data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: In triple NFI cKO MOEs, only dorsal-most zone 1/class I OR genes maintain zonal clustering patterns.
source: Interestingly, while dimensionality reduction and unbiased clustering generated OR clusters that correspond to zonal patterns of OR expression (i.e. each cluster contains OR genes with one zonal identity) in control MOEs, only dorsal-most zone 1/class I OR genes followed this correlation in cKO MOEs (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by spatial transcriptomics data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Conditional triple NFI deletion causes loss of spatial patterning for zone 2–4 OR genes and loss of expression for zone 5 OR genes.
source: Thus, conditional triple NFI deletion causes loss of spatial patterning for zone 2–4 OR genes and loss of expression for zone 5 OR genes, without influencing the expression of zone 1 ORs.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a conclusion from spatial transcriptomics data analysis.

claim: Triple NFI deletion results in an almost complete loss of heterochromatin from ventral ORs and a reduction on zone 3 dorsomedial ORs in ventral OSNs and INPs.
source: ChIP-seq revealed an almost complete loss of heterochromatin from ventral ORs as well as a reduction on zone 3 dorsomedial ORs in NFI cKO ventral OSNs and INPs (Figure 6A, Figure 7—figure supplement 1F–G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1F-G.

claim: Triple NFI deletion results in a strong reduction in the long-range cis and trans genomic contacts made by ventral ORs.
source: Similarly, in situ Hi-C in control and triple NFI cKO OSNs from ventral MOE segments revealed a strong reduction in the long-range cis and trans genomic contacts made by ventral ORs (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Hi-C data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Dorsal ORs did not exhibit strong changes in ChIP-seq and Hi-C contacts upon triple NFI deletion.
source: In contrast, dorsal ORs did not exhibit strong changes in ChIP-seq and Hi-C contacts (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ChIP-seq and Hi-C data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: The patterns of heterochromatin assembly and genomic compartmentalization observed in ventral OSNs upon NFI deletion are similar to those observed in dorsomedial OSNs from control MOEs.
source: Strikingly, in both processes, heterochromatin assembly and genomic compartmentalization, the patterns observed in ventral OSNs upon NFI deletion are similar to those observed in dorsomedial OSNs from the control MOEs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ChIP-seq and Hi-C data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: Triple NFI deletion in ventral INPs results in detection of only dorsal and dorsomedial ORs and depletion of ventral OR identities from the INP transcriptome.
source: Again, as with the results from ChIP-seq and Hi-C experiments, we detect a conversion toward the signatures observed in dorsomedial INPs, i.e., detection of only dorsal and dorsomedial ORs and depletion of ventral OR identities from the INP transcriptome (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Transient induction of Olfr17 transcription in INP/iOSN cells promotes preferential choice of this OR throughout the MOE.
source: Intriguingly, transient induction of Olfr17 transcription promotes preferential choice of this OR throughout the MOE, rather than only in zone 2, where Olfr17 is normally chosen for expression (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The vast majority of mOSNs from zones 1–4 express the INP/iOSN-induced tetO-Olfr17 allele.
source: In fact, the vast majority of mOSNs from zones 1–4 are GFP+, and only in the ventral-most zone 5 we detect a more sporadic pattern of ectopic Olfr17 choice (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7D and E.

claim: Only in the ventral-most zone 5 is there a more sporadic pattern of ectopic Olfr17 choice.
source: In fact, the vast majority of mOSNs from zones 1–4 are GFP+, and only in the ventral-most zone 5 we detect a more sporadic pattern of ectopic Olfr17 choice (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7D and E.

claim: Reduced frequency of ectopic Olfr17 expression in the most ventral segment reflects the fact that heterochromatin levels and genomic compartmentalization of this dorsomedial OR allele is highest at this MOE segment.
source: We hypothesized that reduced frequency of ectopic Olfr17 expression in the most ventral segment reflects the fact that heterochromatin levels and genomic compartmentalization of this dorsomedial OR allele is highest at this MOE segment (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis in the text and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Reducing Olfr17 transcription in INP/iOSN cells with low doxycycline preferentially prohibits ectopic Olfr17 expression in ventral MOE segments.
source: Remarkably, mice that were subjected to this doxycycline regimen continue to frequently express Olfr17 in dorsal mOSNs (zones 1–2), but not in mOSNs from more ventral MOE segments (zones 3–5) (Figure 7D and E), where heterochromatin levels on this OR allele are highest (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7D, E, and F.

claim: The zonal expression of an OR allele in mOSNs can be manipulated by pharmacologically modulating the frequency and levels of transcriptional activation in INP/iOSN cells.
source: Thus, we can manipulate the zonal expression of an OR allele in mOSNs, by pharmacologically modulating the frequency and levels of transcriptional activation in INP/iOSN cells.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a conclusion from the doxycycline experiments.

claim: Polygenic OR transcription in neuronal progenitors highlights a small group of ORs that can be chosen for singular expression later in development.
source: The solution to the perplexing segmentation of the MOE into distinct and reproducible territories of OR expression may be the following: polygenic OR transcription in neuronal progenitors highlights a small group of ORs that can be chosen for singular expression later in development (Figure 7G).
evidence: This is stated in the text as a proposed model and illustrated in Figure 7G.

claim: Heterochromatic silencing preferentially decommissions more dorsal ORs from the mixture of ORs transcribed in progenitors.
source: As these progenitor cells differentiate into iOSNs, heterochromatic silencing may preferentially decommission from this mixture more dorsal ORs, and with lower efficiency, ORs that could be expressed in the segment, biasing this singular choice towards a spatially appropriate OR repertoire (Figure 7G).
evidence: This is stated in the text as a proposed model and illustrated in Figure 7G.

claim: NFI gradients contribute to the silencing of some dorsomedial (primarily zone 3) ORs.
source: We identified gradients of transcription factors NFI A, B, and X as partial orchestrators of the dorsoventral patterning of OR expression, which they establish as follows: they contribute to the silencing of some dorsomedial (primarily zone 3) ORs; they activate both polygenic transcription and silencing of ventral (zone 4 and 5) ORs; and they have no influence on the expression of dorsal-most (class I and zone 1) ORs.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a conclusion from the NFI deletion experiments.

claim: NFI gradients activate both polygenic transcription and silencing of ventral (zone 4 and 5) ORs.
source: We identified gradients of transcription factors NFI A, B, and X as partial orchestrators of the dorsoventral patterning of OR expression, which they establish as follows: they contribute to the silencing of some dorsomedial (primarily zone 3) ORs; they activate both polygenic transcription and silencing of ventral (zone 4 and 5) ORs; and they have no influence on the expression of dorsal-most (class I and zone 1) ORs.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a conclusion from the NFI deletion experiments.

claim: NFI gradients have no influence on the expression of dorsal-most (class I and zone 1) ORs.
source: We identified gradients of transcription factors NFI A, B, and X as partial orchestrators of the dorsoventral patterning of OR expression, which they establish as follows: they contribute to the silencing of some dorsomedial (primarily zone 3) ORs; they activate both polygenic transcription and silencing of ventral (zone 4 and 5) ORs; and they have no influence on the expression of dorsal-most (class I and zone 1) ORs.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a conclusion from the NFI deletion experiments.

claim: Without NFI transcription factors, the majority of the MOE, excluding dorsal-most zone 1, defaults to a zone 2 identity.
source: Without NFI transcription factors, the majority of the MOE, excluding dorsal-most zone 1, defaults to a zone 2 identity.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a conclusion from the NFI deletion experiments.

claim: Triple NFI deletion after the onset of singular OR choice has no effect on OR patterning.
source: Interestingly, triple NFI deletion after the onset of singular OR choice has no effect on OR patterning, consistent with the emerging model that OR specification takes place exclusively at the INP to iOSN transition, and the notion that these patterning factors are not required for maintenance of OR transcription.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by RNA-seq data showing no effect of late NFI deletion.

claim: Singular OR gene choice in OSNs can be executed by the common nucleoprotein complex of Lhx2/Ebf/Ldb1 bound to the multi-enhancer hub.
source: Thus, we speculate that singular OR gene choice in OSNs can be executed by the common nucleoprotein complex of Lhx2/Ebf/Ldb1 bound to the multi-enhancer hub, consistent with the fact that we detect hubs of similar constitution associating with active ORs in different zones (Monahan et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as speculation in the text with a citation to Monahan et al., 2019.

claim: Artificial transcriptional induction of an OR allele in OSN progenitors under the powerful tetO promoter bypasses constraints and results in biased choice of this allele in most mOSNs.
source: Of course, this system has limitations in preserving transcriptional equity: artificial transcriptional induction of an OR allele in OSN progenitors under the powerful tetO promoter bypasses these constraints and results in a biased choice of this allele in most mOSNs.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on the tetO-Olfr17 experiments.

claim: Cis OR regulatory elements are subject to selective pressure that preserves their weak transcriptional activation properties.
source: This immediately suggests that cis OR regulatory elements are subject to selective pressure that preserves their weak transcriptional activation properties, explaining why robust OR transcription in mOSNs requires the assembly of interchromosomal multi-enhancer hubs.
evidence: This is stated as an inference in the text based on the experimental observations.

claim: Mutations on the Lhx2 or Ebf binding sites of the promoter of dorsal OR M71 result in less frequent and more ventral M71 expression patterns.
source: Consistent with this model is the observation that mutations on the Lhx2 or Ebf binding sites of the promoter of dorsal OR M71 result in less frequent and more ventral M71 expression patterns (Rothman et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Rothman et al., 2005.

claim: DV segmentation of the MOE may serve as a mechanism that prevents ORs with stronger differences in promoter strength from competing for singular expression.
source: Thus, DV segmentation of the MOE may serve as a mechanism that prevents ORs with stronger differences in promoter strength from competing for singular expression, assuring that every OR is expressed at meaningful, for odor perception, frequencies.
evidence: This is stated as a proposed mechanism in the text.

claim: Zonal regulation assures that ORs are expressed in a reproducibly patterned fashion in the MOE.
source: In addition, as our spatial transcriptomic data showed, zonal regulation assures that ORs are expressed in a reproducibly patterned fashion in the MOE.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on spatial transcriptomics data.

claim: In wild-type mice, unbiased machine learning approaches identify at least five distinct OR expression patterns.
source: While in wild-type mice unbiased machine learning approaches identify at least five distinct OR expression patterns, in the triple NFI cKO mice these patterns become intermixed for all but zone 1 ORs.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on spatial transcriptomics data analysis.

claim: In triple NFI cKO mice, OR expression patterns become intermixed for all but zone 1 ORs.
source: While in wild-type mice unbiased machine learning approaches identify at least five distinct OR expression patterns, in the triple NFI cKO mice these patterns become intermixed for all but zone 1 ORs.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on spatial transcriptomics data analysis.

claim: Individual mitral cells have patterned projections in the brain.
source: With recent observations arguing that individual mitral cells, the second-order neurons in the olfactory circuit, have patterned projections in the brain (Chen et al., 2022), non-random OR expression in the MOE may contribute to putative hardwired components of odor perception and valence (Kobayakawa et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2022 and Kobayakawa et al., 2007.

claim: OR gene silencing is highest in the very cells that express ORs.
source: A peculiar feature of the OR gene family that had emerged from our past work is that OR gene silencing is highest in the very cells that express ORs (Magklara et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Magklara et al., 2011.

claim: Both H3K9me3/H3K79me3 and genomic compartmentalization in each MOE segment are strongest on OR groups that are transcriptionally active during OSN differentiation.
source: Our zonal analysis further strengthened this intriguing correlation, as both H3K9me3/H3K79me3 and genomic compartmentalization in each MOE segment are strongest on OR groups that are transcriptionally active during OSN differentiation.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on ChIP-seq and Hi-C data analysis.

claim: Early OR transcription is the signal for both genomic silencing and singular choice.
source: A fascinating implication of this observation is that early OR transcription is the signal for both genomic silencing and singular choice.
evidence: This is stated as an implication in the text based on the observed correlations.

claim: Strong transcriptional induction of Olfr17 at the INP/iOSN stage results in strong recruitment of the Greek Island hub and stable choice of this OR allele in most mOSNs throughout the MOE.
source: Although the former is only implied by the strong correlation between OR transcription in OSN progenitors and genomic silencing, the latter is experimentally supported by the striking observation that strong transcriptional induction of Olfr17 at the INP/iOSN stage results in strong recruitment of the Greek Island hub, and stable choice of this OR allele in most mOSNs throughout the MOE.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Hi-C and expression data from the tetO-Olfr17 experiments.

claim: The timing and levels of transcriptional induction could be the arbiters between genomic silencing and singular choice.
source: We propose that the timing and levels of transcriptional induction could be the arbiters between genomic silencing and singular choice.
evidence: This is stated as a proposal in the text based on the experimental observations.

claim: ORs that are transcribed first in the INP stage are most likely to be silenced.
source: ORs that are transcribed first in the INP stage, when the Greek Island hub cannot yet form due to the continuous expression of Lamin b receptor (Clowney et al., 2012), are most likely to be silenced.
evidence: This is stated in the text as part of a proposed model with a citation to Clowney et al., 2012.

claim: OR alleles activated during the assembly of the multi-enhancer hub may compete for hub recruitment.
source: OR alleles activated during the assembly of the multi-enhancer hub, at the INP to iOSN transition, may compete for hub recruitment.
evidence: This is stated in the text as part of a proposed model.

claim: The OR allele that first associates with a multi-enhancer hub will be stably protected from heterochromatic silencing.
source: The OR allele that will first associate with a multi-enhancer hub will be stably protected from heterochromatic silencing, possibly due to the significantly increased rates of OR transcription, whereas the other co-transcribed ORs will succumb to heterochromatic silencing.
evidence: This is stated in the text as part of a proposed model.

claim: Singular OR transcription may not depend on the silencing of every single OR in the genome.
source: In other words, singular OR transcription may not depend on the silencing of every single OR in the genome: by encoding silencing and stable choice with the same exact molecular feature, OSNs choose one and silence a small fraction of the whole OR repertoire in each nucleus—the rest are not relevant.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a conclusion from the proposed model.

claim: This study constitutes a refinement of the original model which proposed that all but one OR allele become silenced in each OSN.
source: Notably, this constitutes a refinement of our original model, which proposed that all but one OR allele become silenced in each OSN (Magklara et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation to the original model (Magklara et al., 2011).

claim: Cells expressing the INP/iOSN-induced tetO-Olfr17 allele do not express any other OR genes.
source: Consistent with this, cells expressing the tetO-Olfr17 allele do not express any other OR genes (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Treating tetO-Olfr17; Gng8-tTA mice with high doxycycline for 35 days fails to extinguish tetO-Olfr17 expression in mOSNs.
source: Furthermore, treating tetO-Olfr17; Gng8-tTA mice with high doxycycline (200 mg/kg in food) for 35 days fails to extinguish tetO-Olfr17 expression in mOSNs (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B–C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B-C.

claim: Greek Islands are recruited specifically to the tetO-Olfr17 allele in OSNs where this allele was induced in progenitors.
source: Indeed, Hi-C experiments of these OSNs revealed that Greek Islands, the intergenic OR enhancers that converge over the chosen OR allele (Lomvardas et al., 2006; Markenscoff-Papadimitriou et al., 2014; Monahan et al., 2019), are recruited specifically to the tetO-Olfr17 allele (Figure 7C), explaining the sustained expression of this OR in mOSNs.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Hi-C data shown in Figure 7C, with citations to previous studies.

claim: Gng8 is expressed in INPs and iOSNs and completely shuts off in mOSNs.
source: Gng8 is expressed in INPs and iOSNs, and completely shuts off in mOSNs (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by expression data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D.
